transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, i am the AE on your account and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:07] Daniel Kim: good, thanks, Daniel here. we wanted to focus today on your console tracing and request logs, specifically how we can debug some flaky outputs and latency spikes we've been seeing in prod.
[00:00:18] Priya Nair: great, thanks Daniel. quick agenda, i'll demo the tracing UI, show error analysis, how request logs map back to traces, and then a debugging flow we usually use for root cause. sound ok?
[00:00:30] Maria Lopez: yep that's perfect, we have some SRE constraints and audit requirements so we'll ask about retention and exports.
[00:00:38] Alex Chen: quick qual — can you remind us where you're running your inference today? hosted api or on-prem / private?
[00:00:44] Ethan Park: currently using a mix, prod is hosted with OpenAI for a lot of user-facing flows, and we have some internal POCs on GCP vm endpoints. we're exploring moving some sensitive workloads to dedicated or private.
[00:00:56] Priya Nair: ok that makes sense. when you say flaky outputs, is this hallucination-style or timeouts/errors?
[00:01:03] Daniel Kim: mostly inconsistent outputs on the summarization endpoint — sometimes it drops sections — and occasional 5xxs during peak.
[00:01:12] Priya Nair: thanks. i'll start screen share — i'm in the Redwood Console. first, the Traces tab — we sample requests by default and you can increase sampling on a route, or instrument client-side to send full traces for a short window. most customers do 1% always + ramp to 10% for debugging.
[00:01:30] [screen share noise] Priya Nair: here you see a trace timeline, latency by stage (network, tokenize, model-output), and an event stream with model variants used, cache hits, and fallbacks. note: sometimes the transcript shows "KV cash" in the auto-gen logs — that's our ASR hiccup but you get the idea (we mean KV cache).
[00:01:51] Maria Lopez: can you map a trace to our request id in logs? we correlate by our internal request_id header.
[00:01:57] Priya Nair: yes, we index request_id headers automatically if you configure them — in the Request Logs page you can filter by request_id and jump to the corresponding trace. let me show that — filtering: request_id=atlas-req-1347.
[00:02:12] [pause] Priya Nair: there, you can see the exact tokens generated and the model variant used, plus the kv-cache hit rate — looks like this request had a cold cache which increased latency.
[00:02:24] Daniel Kim: that cold cache note is helpful, our usage has bursts after an hourly job. can we pre-warm or pin models?
[00:02:31] Priya Nair: for Dedicated you can reserve capacity and keep warmed workers; for hosted you can enable reserved concurrency and a warmup policy. we also recommend prefix caching for recurrent user sessions.
[00:02:45] Ethan Park: what's the quantization story — does that change traces or cause more errors?
[00:02:50] Priya Nair: quantization changes numeric traces slightly but we surface model-variant in the trace so you can see if a q4 or int8 variant was used; some customers see minor tokenization differences but it's rare to cause semantic regressions.
[00:03:05] Maria Lopez: about retention — we need logs/audit for 90 days for HIPAA-adjacent workflows. how does Redwood handle export and retention?
[00:03:13] Alex Chen: we have configurable retention for request logs and traces on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has tiered retention — 30/90/365 days as an add-on. exports are via S3 or BigQuery for longer-term storage. we'll send the security docs with the exact retention options.
[00:03:32] Daniel Kim: do you have SOC 2 and an iso cert?
[00:03:35] Alex Chen: yes SOC 2 Type II, and we're in progress on ISO 27001 — i'll include cert links.
[00:03:43] Priya Nair: back to the debugging flow — step 1: filter request logs for the failing route and timeframe, step 2: open the trace to inspect model latency and fallbacks, step 3: look at input/response diffs and prompt truncations. here's an example where a prompt was truncated at 4096 tokens and the model returned a truncated summary.
[00:04:05] [00:04:05] Maria Lopez: our tokenizer is custom, will the token counts match?
[00:04:10] Priya Nair: token counts are shown per model variant, if you use a custom tokenizer we recommend instrumenting the client to send the token_count header so traces reflect your tokenizer.
[00:04:21] Ethan Park: what about automated regression alerts? we saw a spike last week but didn't get notified.
[00:04:26] Priya Nair: Console has quality monitors — you can attach eval tests to a route and get alerts on metric regressions (ROUGE, exact-match, custom heuristics). we can configure an eval set using your failing prompts and send regression emails or webhook alerts.
[00:04:44] Alex Chen: quick interjection on cost — increasing tracing sampling increases observability cost. our Optimize team can recommend sampling strategies to reduce unit cost while preserving signal.
[00:04:57] Daniel Kim: can you show the error analysis view?
[00:05:00] Priya Nair: sure, switching to Error analysis — we group errors by signature (5xx, timeout, model-fallback) and surface the top failing prompts. here's an example cluster where the model hit a fallback to a smaller variant under load and produced a terse reply.
[00:05:16] [crosstalk] Maria Lopez: is fallback configurable? we don't want silent model downgrades.
[00:05:21] Priya Nair: yes, you can set strict routing policies to avoid automatic fallback, or set canary fallback thresholds. we also log fallback reason codes in traces.
[00:05:33] Daniel Kim: how do you handle PII in traces?
[00:05:36] Alex Chen: sensitive fields can be redacted at ingest, and on Private you can disable trace storage entirely, or store encrypted traces using your KMS. we'll include the KMS/HSM integration doc.
[00:05:50] Ethan Park: any limitations on request-log export size? we generate high QPS, like 2k req/s at peaks.
[00:05:57] Priya Nair: for high QPS, we recommend sampling and streaming exports to S3/BigQuery; Dedicated gives higher throughput for exports. we also have backpressure controls to avoid exporter overload.
[00:06:12] [00:06:12] Priya Nair: demoing the Request Logs page now — you can search by route, model, status, latency buckets, and custom headers. here's a filter for status:5xx and latency>1s. selecting a log entry surfaces the trace id and you can click through.
[00:06:29] Daniel Kim: nice. can we get a csv of request logs for a specific date range?
[00:06:33] Priya Nair: yes, export to CSV or JSON lines, and for bulk we recommend the export job to S3; the UI will generate ad-hoc exports up to a couple million rows depending on plan.
[00:06:46] Maria Lopez: what about live tailing during an incident?
[00:06:49] Priya Nair: we have a live tail with tailing and alerting — you can pipe matches to webhooks or Slack. it's handy for on-call during deploys.
[00:06:59] Ethan Park: curious about mapping from trace to model inputs — is the full input stored?
[00:07:04] Priya Nair: by default we store full inputs in traces but you can configure redaction rules to mask PHI/PII. again on Private you can choose not to store inputs at all.
[00:07:14] [00:07:14] Alex Chen: question for timeline — are you aiming to start a pilot this quarter?
[00:07:19] Daniel Kim: yes we'd like to run a pilot in october, with a focus on the summarization route and a benchmark of 10k requests.
[00:07:27] Alex Chen: great, we can scope a pilot with Dedicated trial capacity or a hosted pilot with increased sampling. i'll include both options in the proposal.
[00:07:35] Maria Lopez: any gotchas on billing for exports and tracing?
[00:07:38] Alex Chen: exports and tracing incur extra storage/ingest fees; it's all itemized in the proposal. we usually structure a pilot budget to include trace sampling and exports for the test window.
[00:07:50] [00:07:50] Priya Nair: now i want to show a real debugging flow — here's a failing request we reproduced: open the trace, check tokenization, confirm fallback reason code, check model variant differences, then correlate with request logs to see if similar failures cluster by user or time.
[00:08:08] [sound of typing] Priya Nair: here's a cluster view — you can export top 100 examples into an eval set and run automatic comparisons across model variants.
[00:08:20] Ethan Park: that eval set — can it run nightly? we want daily regression checks.
[00:08:24] Priya Nair: yes scheduled evals are supported; you can set cadence and notification channels.
[00:08:31] Daniel Kim: regarding SSO, we use Okta and need SCIM provisioning + role-based access.
[00:08:36] Alex Chen: we support SAML SSO + SCIM and granular RBAC; we'll include a quickstart for Okta.
[00:08:44] Maria Lopez: one more — if we move to Private, what's the uplift for observability features?
[00:08:49] Priya Nair: Private includes the same Console features, but you run the control plane in your VPC and you can opt for local retention and KMS. there is an uplift for deployment/support — details in the pricing doc.
[00:08:59] [00:08:59] Daniel Kim: ok thanks this is super helpful. can we recap next steps?
[00:09:04] Alex Chen: sure — i'll send pricing + pilot options, Priya to share trace sampling guide and request-log export docs, and Atlas to provide failing prompts. we'll target pilot in october.
[00:09:15] Maria Lopez: noted. thanks everyone.
[00:09:18] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up by email.
[00:09:22] [call ends — note: remaining 45 minutes were a live walkthrough and Q&A; Fireflies captured key snippets here for brevity.]
